hints: Focus on which atom is electron poor in the carbonyl group and what the real nucleophile is when KCN is present.
Remember that $\text{CN}^-$ has a lone pair on carbon that attacks the $\delta+$ carbonyl carbon first, pushing the $\pi$ electrons up onto oxygen.
Think about what is left after that first attack, an $\text{O}^-$ alkoxide, and how it can pick up $\text{H}^+$ from a weak acid like HCN to finish.
walkthrough:
**Spot the polar carbonyl**

Butanone has a polar $\text{C=O}$ bond. Oxygen is more electronegative, so we get $\text{C}^{\delta+}$ and $\text{O}^{\delta-}$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}^{\delta+}=\text{O}^{\delta-}\text{CH}_3$$

**Identify the true nucleophile**

HCN is a weak acid and a poor nucleophile. The little KCN provides $\text{CN}^-$, which has a lone pair on carbon and is a strong nucleophile.

**First move is nucleophilic attack**

The lone pair from $\text{CN}^-$ attacks the $\delta+$ carbon. The $\pi$ bond breaks and both electrons move onto oxygen to give an alkoxide intermediate.

$$\text{C=O} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{C(CN)-O}^-$$

**Second move is protonation**

The strongly basic $\text{O}^-$ then accepts $\text{H}^+$ from HCN. This gives the cyanohydrin product and regenerates $\text{CN}^-$.

$$\text{C(CN)-O}^- + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{C(CN)-OH} + \text{CN}^-$$

options.A: Incorrect. The $\pi$ bond does not accept $\text{H}^+$ first. Protonation of the carbonyl is not the first step under basic KCN conditions, nucleophilic attack by $\text{CN}^-$ comes first.
options.B: Incorrect. The nucleophile is the lone pair on carbon in $\text{CN}^-$, not a $\pi$ bond pair from $\text{CN}^-$. Also the second step protonates the negatively charged $\text{O}^-$, not neutral O.
options.C: Incorrect. This describes acid-catalysed addition where O is protonated first. Here KCN makes the solution basic, so $\text{CN}^-$ attacks first and protonation happens last.
options.D: Correct. A lone pair from $\text{CN}^-$ attacks the $\delta+$ carbonyl carbon to form a $\text{C-CN}$ bond and an $\text{O}^-$ intermediate, then $\text{O}^-$ accepts $\text{H}^+$ from HCN to give the cyanohydrin.
